# 1 Enoch Chapter 75 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn-astr (Aramaic) | **Section:** Astronomical Book (Book of Luminaries)

---

**1** The angelic commanders in charge of the entire creation and all the stars also have responsibility for the four extra days — they are inseparable from their duty according to the yearly reckoning. These angels serve during the four days that fall outside the regular yearly count.

**2** Because of this arrangement, people make errors in their reckoning. For those luminaries truly serve at the fixed stations of the world — one in the first gate, one in the third gate of heaven, one in the fourth gate, and one in the sixth gate — and in this way the year's exact count of three hundred and sixty-four days is achieved.

**3** The angel Uriel showed me all this — the signs, the appointed times, the years, and the days. The Lord of glory has set Uriel in permanent charge over all the lights of heaven, both in heaven and on earth, so that they govern the face of the sky and are visible on earth, serving as the leaders of day and night: the sun, the moon, the stars, and all the ministering beings who travel in the heavenly chariots.

**4** Uriel also showed me twelve portals open in the circuit of the sun's chariot in the sky, through which the sun's rays break out. From these portals warmth spreads across the earth when they are opened at their proper seasons.

**5** And likewise for the winds — the spirit of the dew, of clouds, and of the mist that settles over the earth and dwells in it —

**6** and in the same way the spirit of rain and dew descends from its dwelling place. Through all of these, the pattern of their motion is consistent in both winter and summer.

**7** I also saw twelve portals open in the sky, from which the winds blow out, and from which dew, rain, mist, frost, snow, and hail pour down on the earth.

**8** In seven of these portals, cold dominated — two and a half portions each. In the remaining five portals were elements of warmth and cold together, along with dew, rain, winds, and storms.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Chapter 75 explains the four intercalary days — strategically placed at the solstices and equinoxes in the 364-day calendar to mark the four seasons. The twelve portals of the sun's heat and the twelve portals of wind and weather form a comprehensive cosmological system. Uriel is the supreme angelic administrator of all natural phenomena.*
